01 / SERVICES

Engineering help where the work gets technical.

Start with the infrastructure and the way things operate today. The platform layer is the same whatever you end up running on it; the AI work on top of it is the specialisation. We scope the engagement around a decision, an integration or a result you need to show, with clear responsibilities and evidence that it works.

F / IO
02// OFFER

What we deliver

Four services, scoped to what you already run.

Each one can be a standalone engagement or a stage of a larger delivery. The platform work comes first because everything else sits on it. We agree responsibilities and acceptance criteria before implementation begins.

  1. 01

    Kubernetes and infrastructure

    We design and deliver the platform your applications need, including Kubernetes and GPU infrastructure. It is built to carry whatever you run on it rather than one workload in particular. Capacity, recovery, upgrades and day-to-day ownership are part of the design. We start with the systems you already run.

  2. 02

    Enterprise AI

    Tell us what you want AI to do for the business. We help define the scope, choose an approach and build it into your existing environment. Our work covers model selection, system integration, testing and deployment.

  3. 03

    Knowledge systems

    Make your organisation's information useful to AI. We help establish which sources to trust, who can access them and how to keep them current. That gives the search and answer system a clear set of requirements to work against.

  4. 04

    AI governance

    Decide what AI may do on its own and when a person needs to approve the next step. We design controls around those decisions, including access, review and how to handle failures. The scope includes how those controls will be tested.

03// GOVERNANCE

Governance, shown rather than described

An instruction is a request. A permission is a fact.

This is what the AI governance service produces: a decision made before the action runs, not a rule written into a prompt and hoped for. The illustration below is the shape of that control, not a product you buy.

Illustrative evidence: identity workflow-agent-17, the target and revision, the policy decision, and what the approval actually covered. After a real action you still compare what happened against what was approved, and reconcile any difference.

A restart of production/payment-api by workflow-agent-17, which is authorized only for staging/*, is refused. A human approval naming that target, the restart operation and revision 182 permits that one request and nothing else. Identity and permissions come from the execution layer, never from what the model claims about itself.

04// ESCALATION

What reaches a person

Send people the cases that genuinely need a person.

AI handles the volume; people handle the judgment. What gets escalated is written down as a rule during design, so nobody is asked to trust a confidence score without seeing the evidence behind it.

  • 01

    Normal result

    Runs under the policy already approved.

  • 02

    High-value transaction

    Always goes to a person.

  • 03

    Missing evidence or conflicting data

    Stops and asks someone accountable.

  • 04

    Low confidence

    Escalates instead of guessing.

  • 05

    Against policy

    Blocked, then routed to review.

  • 06

    Wide blast radius

    Needs explicit approval first.

05// ARCHITECTURE

Where the controls sit

Keep model choice separate from authority.

Agents can run on local, enterprise-hosted or frontier models. Identity, authorization, scope, approval, tool access, state, audit and reconciliation are checked before any of them reach your systems. Choosing a different model does not change who is allowed to do what.

06// ONGOING

After it ships

AI workflows need maintenance, not just a launch.

Review the corrections people made, the outputs they rejected, the escalations and exceptions, how long things take and what changed in the data and the business rules. AI can propose improvements, but every change is tested, reviewed and released as a controlled revision. Production policy never changes quietly. Ongoing support is agreed separately, per project.
